sentences.text: Rajesh .....Applicant(s) Versus State of U.P. .....Opposite Party(s) Counsel for Applicant(s) :
Shikhar Tandon Counsel for Opposite Party(s) :
G.A. Hon'Ble Krishan Pahal, J. 1.
List has been revised.
Supplementary affidavit filed by learned counsel for the applicant today is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Shikhar Tandon, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Durgvijay Singh, learned A.A.G., assisted by Sri Sunil Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.
This is the second bail application.
The first bail application was rejected by this Court vide order dated 26.07.2024.
4. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 297 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Babina, District Jhansi, during the pendency of trial.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged in the FIR.

6. Learned counsel has further stated that Fundamental Rights of the applicant enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution of India stands violated as he is languishing in jail since 04.09.2022, as such he has been incarcerated for more than three years.

7. Learned counsel has further submitted that the applicant had conducted the last rites of the deceased person which indicates that he was a bonafide person and has nothing to do with the said suicide committed by the deceased person.
The deceased was undergoing coaching of CTET examination and all the expenses were being borne by the applicant.

8. Learned counsel has next stated that it has come up in the statement of PW-2 that sister of the deceased person Reeta also used to live in the very same house with the deceased person and she has not been made witness in the said case as it was the said sister of the deceased person only who could have brought truth before the court, as such the applicant is entitled for bail.
The Investigating Officer is not turning up despite coercive measures being taken by the court.
9. The applicant has no criminal history.

In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse Rajesh vs State Of U.P. on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3974284/
1 the liberty of bail and shall cooperate with trial.

10. Per contra, learned A.A.G. has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that six witnesses have been examined to date and the trial is at its conclusive end, as such the applicant is not entitled for bail.

11. The Supreme Court in case of X Vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr. reported in 2024 INSC 909, has held that once the trial has commenced, it should be allowed to reach to its final conclusion, which may either result in conviction or acquittal of the accused.

entities.text: X Vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr. reported in 2024 INSC 909
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail should not be normally granted to the accused after the charge has been framed.
It should also not be granted by looking into the discrepancies here or there in the deposition.

12. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and also considering the status of trial being at its conclusive end, I do not find it a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
13. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected.

14. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously, in view of the principle laid down in the recent judgements of the Supreme Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.

sentences.text: 15. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
